description: One invented earlier session in the email digital twin (Northwind Mail), as a confirmed Work Map. Loaded only when AGENT_SEED_MAPS=1 and no confirmed map exists; in memory only, never written to the maps file. Synthetic data: every name, address and quote is made up. No screen moments: nothing here was recorded. The main demo's customer_07 rule is never seeded: it is learned live.

processes.title: Invoice email: payment terms
processes.summary: Send a customer their invoice by email with the payment terms their agreement allows.

steps.action: Opened the draft "Invoice INV-2188" to billing@harbor-print.example in Northwind Mail; the last line of the message said "Payment terms: Net 14."

steps.goal: Check which customer the invoice is for
steps.action: Read the recipient and the subject, then looked the customer up in the list of signed agreements

steps.goal: Set the payment terms the customer is entitled to
steps.action: Changed "Net 14" to "Net 30" in the last line of the message

decision.summary: Net 30 instead of the standard Net 14 for a customer with a signed agreement
decision.reason: The customer has a signed agreement for Net 30
decision.quote: Harbor Print has a signed agreement, so it gets Net 30. The standard is Net 14.

steps.action: Pressed Send with the invoice PDF attached and the agreed terms in the last line

guardrails.condition: Payment terms longer than the standard Net 14 on an invoice email
guardrails.requiredAction: Net 30 only for a customer with a signed agreement; anything longer than Net 30 needs the finance lead
guardrails.reason: Only customers with a signed agreement are entitled to longer terms
guardrails.quote: If they have a signed agreement it is Net 30. Anything longer, I ask the finance lead first.
exceptions: A customer without a signed agreement keeps the standard Net 14

map.teachBack: Here is what I understood. Invoice emails use the standard Net 14. A customer with a signed agreement gets Net 30, and anything longer needs the finance lead. Is that right?
